newsitem.title: USA: New York State comptroller sues Columbia/HCA execs.
newsitem.headline: New York State comptroller sues Columbia/HCA execs.

text.p: New York State's comptroller said Thursday he had filed suit against 11 present or former officials of Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp, alleging they had put the value of the company's stock at risk.
New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall is also the sole trustee of New York State's pension fund, which owns over 2.6 million Columbia/HCA shares.
A spokeswoman for McCall said that despite the lawsuit, he had no plans to sell the pension fund's Columbia/HCA shares.
Columbia/HCA is under investigation by a number of federal agencies probing possible fraud against the Medicare program.
Three company executives have been indicted on charges of defrauding the federal government, Columbia/HCA has undergone a management shake-up, and its stock price has suffered.
McCall said in a statement that the Columbia/HCA stock held by the New York State and Local Retirement Systems was worth about $86 million.
His suit, filed in federal court in Tennessee, names 11 present or former directors or senior officials of the company, which is based in Nashville, Tenn.
The suit alleges the officials failed in their responsibilities to Columbia/HCA shareholders.

The suit alleges, "As a result of the wrongful conduct undertaken by defendants, the company has suffered, and will continue to suffer, damages through legal fees, fines, penalities, lost revenues and securities fraud damanges."

It continues, "In addition, Columbia's reputation has been injured, and its credit rating and stock value have suffered...Those injuries should be borne by the individual defendants, not by the company."

The suit is one of the stiffest steps McCall has taken recently against a corporation. He has also campaigned for resolutions at tobacco companies against smoking by teenagers, and has raised concerns about the impact on Texaco Inc's stock of a race discrimination case.
